Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the closing plenary of the Robotic Surgery Summit. My name is Ken Walsh, and I'm chairing this last session. Before we start, a little housekeeping. Each speaker has five minutes for a final reflection, and after that, we'll take questions from the floor. Our first speaker is a nurse from Einstein Hospital in Sao Paulo. Three years ago, her team had never worked with a robot. Today, their setup time is about half of what it was, and two other centers in Brazil are collecting the same data. She is going to share what she learned, in hindsight, and what comes next. Please welcome Andreia Heins.

Thank you, Ken. When I first stood at a podium in English, I had prepared every word, and I was still very nervous. In hindsight, the problem was not my English. I was trying to be perfect, not clear. So here is my insight from this summit. A robotic program does not grow because of the robot. It grows when the team keeps the momentum, year after year. Although our results are good, it seems that the real work starts now. Next year, we would like to scale up to two more hospitals, provided that their nurses train with our team first. And on a personal note, today I gave this whole talk in English, and I felt like myself. Thank you.
